parsed.attack: The invitation goes to a sibling being asked to join a record whose explicit purpose is to establish who has been paying more, which is the live grievance in the family rather than a neutral utility: the sibling paying less has an affirmative reason to stay out, and the sibling paying more already has the spreadsheet. The cycle is a bill, so one turn takes a month at best, and the idea's own kill line - 40% adding a second sibling within 30 days - sets the ceiling coefficient at 0.4 on a 30-day cycle inside a graph that closes at three or four people and never touches another household. Nobody types 'Medicaid lookback documentation' into the App Store, so the roughly 65% of downloads that come from store search is simply unavailable here.
parsed.strongest_defence: Medicaid lookback is a keyword with a real, motivated, free congregation - elder-law attorneys' comment sections, r/Medicaid, r/AgingParents - and a family that has just learned a five-year lookback is coming has a deadline-grade reason to onboard every sibling at once.
parsed.verdict_reason: The invite loop turns at most 0.4 on a 30-day cycle inside a graph that closes at one family and never reaches the next household.
